catalog_quote: Stress is phonemic in Nuaulu but it carries a light functional load. Primary stress generally occurs on the penultimate syllable of a bisyllabic word-root and does not shift with the addition or deletion of affixes. audit.action: check whether this is the same language as another entry
audit.recode_to: Re-key this StressTyp2-derived record from nort2867 (North Nuaulu) to sout2895 (South Nuaulu) and merge it with the existing sout2895 'Nuaulu' record, which rests on the identical Bolton 1989 pp.102-103 but is coded 'morphological' (root-penult, affixes invisible) whereas this one is coded 'fixed-dominant' with a word-penult template penultimate stress. Bolton's own data (['raka-ne], [ka-'rana-te], ['sani-ku] = surface antepenult) contradict a word-penult template; the merged record should carry the root-anchored coding (the sout2895 reading), and the 'contra' text should say StressTyp2's 'penultimate' misses the root domain, not that the source calls stress 'lexical'.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: confirmed verbatim on the page image we hold and scanned of Bolton 1989 printed p.102/103 (PDF pp.111-112). (2) Source: a 1989 SIL workpaper phonology (31 pp) from primary fieldwork; the only larger work is the same author's offline 1990 MA thesis, so the held source is probably the best obtainable and nothing found suggests the stress facts are wrong. (3) The problem is identity, not evidence: Bolton 1989 p.90 explicitly describes the SOUTHERN dialect (Rouhua, Kec. Amahai) = Glottolog sout2895 [nxl]; our overlay map (overlay/: 'North Nuaulu (Bolton's Nuaulu); variety uncertain') put the StressTyp2 entry on nort2867 [nni], a dormant northern variety with zero descriptive references, which Bolton says differs phonologically and was not studied. The catalog therefore holds two records for one description -- nort2867 'fixed-dominant' (word-penult template) and sout2895 '

sources.note: Only grammar-length description of (South) Nuaulu, by the same fieldworker; would settle the two points our the primary-stress rule leaves open (secondary-stress domain root-initial vs word-initial; behaviour of monosyllabic roots under prefixation) and confirm the affix-invariant root-penult rule with more morphology than the one-page 1989 section.
